topic: Minato named his son Naruto after reading Jiraiya's novel inspired by Nagato, making the Child of Prophecy's name trace back to another Child of Prophecy
title: Nagato's Name Lives On In Naruto
description: Jiraiya wrote "The Tale of the Utterly Gutsy Shinobi" inspired by Nagato's words about finding peace. The novel barely sold, but one reader bought it: a young shinobi named Minato. Years later, Minato named his son Naruto after that book—meaning the name of the Child of Prophecy traces directly back to Jiraiya's first chosen one.
comment: Would Naruto even exist with his famous name if Jiraiya had never met Nagato?

lines.text: After three years with Nagato, Jiraiya sat down and wrote a novel inspired by one sentence the boy had said.

shot.fallback: mentor writing late into the night

lines.text: Nagato had promised that someday he would find a real path to peace, even though he didn't know how yet.

shot.search: Nagato promises path to peace vow
shot.fallback: hopeful child making a quiet promise

lines.text: Jiraiya called the book The Tale of the Utterly Gutsy Shinobi and dedicated it to Nagato by name in chapter 446.

shot.fallback: finished novel dedicated to a young student

lines.text: The novel barely sold at all. Most readers ignored it completely. Except for one.

shot.fallback: young ninja discovering an overlooked book

lines.text: A young jonin named Minato Namikaze bought a copy, and he couldn't put it down.

shot.fallback: young shinobi reading with quiet focus

lines.text: Years later, when Minato had a son, he named him Naruto—directly after the character in Jiraiya's book.

shot.fallback: parent choosing a name with meaning

lines.text: The Child of Prophecy's name came from a book inspired by Jiraiya's first Child of Prophecy.
Nagato's influence shaped the name of the boy who would forgive him...

shot.fallback: two chosen ones connected across time
